Pallotti High splits leadership roles, names first female lay principal

RORY CAHILL
August 20, 2026
Pallotti High School
Catherine Edwards is the new principal of St. Vincent Pallotti High School.
Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 3:04
Instaread

St. Vincent Pallotti High School has adopted a new leadership structure with separate principal and president roles, a major change for the 105-year-old private Catholic school.

Jeffrey Palumbo, who held both offices for the past 14 years, is president under the new structure, while assistant principal Catherine Edwards has been promoted to principal. Edwards is the first female layperson [someone who is not a member of the clergy] to serve as principal of Pallotti High School.

“I’m going to handle the day to day,” Edwards said. “And I’m going to ask him to go out and fundraise to support what we’re doing here.”

Palumbo said it was time for a change in the school’s leadership. 

“What we have been doing is not the traditional leadership structure,” he said. “I was president-principal for 14 years, and it’s time for some new energy and new ideas.”

Edwards said her priorities include adding SAT and ACT preparation to the curriculum, increasing parental engagement and renovating classrooms and other facilities. She said the transition should be “seamless” for students because of her long history at the school and connection to the community.

A South Bend, Indiana, native, Edwards earned a psychology degree from the University of Notre Dame and a master’s degree in Catholic school leadership and guidance counseling from Catholic University before working there as an admissions counselor and transfer student adviser. She has lived in the Washington area for 36 years and now resides in Gaithersburg.

Before returning to education, Edwards ran an animal rescue nonprofit, where her family fostered more than 400 puppies and kittens. She continues to volunteer at a local animal shelter.

“Running a non-profit permitted me to put my business and people skills to work,” Edwards said. “Every day was different, just as it is when you run a school.”

Edwards has three children. Her oldest son, Vincent, died from a brain tumor in 2005, and her husband died of cancer three years ago.

“I am very blessed to have a wonderful support system and [I] really try to channel my losses into something positive,” Edwards said, “like working with young people and their families [or homeless animals].”

While raising her children, Edwards volunteered at St. Jane de Chantal School in Bethesda and later served four years on its board, including as president.

Edwards joined Pallotti in 2018 as dean of students before becoming assistant principal and now principal. She said separating the leadership roles will allow her to focus on the school’s day-to-day operations while Palumbo concentrates on fundraising, donor relations and working with the board of directors.

“When Mr. Palumbo held, for 14 years, the combined position, that is a lot for one person to do,” Edwards said. “His focus on principal duties meant he had less time available for outward-facing work, such as fundraising.”

Jacqui Gilmer, a parent of two Pallotti students, expressed confidence in both Palumbo and Edwards.

“I know the kids are very fond of Ms. Edwards,” she said. “It’ll be interesting to see how it plays out.”
